# Voice regression fixtures

These WAV files are synthetic test speech, never microphone recordings. The original clips are described by
[clips.json](clips.json) and generated by `scripts/voice/prepare.mjs --update-fixtures`.

## Unfinished wake checks (10 November 2026)

`wake_question.wav` and `wake_question_repeat.wav` preserve two failing inputs for **listening-ci-r7-1** (the early
scratch investigation called it listening-diagnostic-r7-1). Their text is “Hey Ember, what's on my screen?”.
The first partial check transcribed “Hey, Amber, what's up?”; the other produced a hyphenated decoder repeat.
Both finished audio clips transcribe the intended name. Preserve these fixed bytes: a fresh synthesis is random
and does not promise the same recognizer failure. [wake-diagnostic.json](wake-diagnostic.json) pins the files and
source configuration. The tests also retain all six original negative clips.

Generation used the repository's existing **Piper Amy low** test speaker, prepared with the archive URL and SHA-256
in `scripts/voice/prepare.mjs` (`c70f5284a09a7fd4ed203b39b2ff51cac1432b422b852eb647b481dade3cf639`).
With sherpa-onnx 1.13.8, `createOfflineTts` uses that speaker's `en_US-amy-low.onnx`, `tokens.txt` and
`espeak-ng-data`, `numThreads: 1`, `debug: 0`, `maxNumSentences: 1`. The call is
`tts.generate({ text: "Hey Ember, what's on my screen?", sid: 0, speed: 0.9 })`. Prepend 9,600 zero samples
(0.6 seconds at 16kHz), then write with `sherpa.writeWave(file, { samples, sampleRate: 16000 })`.
The captures are renderings 0 and 2 of the first speed in the five-rendering evaluation-shaped investigation.
No production model, wake word, speaker identity or threshold was changed to create them.

The pinned Amy archive's `MODEL_CARD` credits [MycroftAI/mimic3-voices](https://github.com/MycroftAI/mimic3-voices)
and gives its dataset licence as “See URL”. That upstream repository supplies **Creative Commons
Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International** ([licence](https://github.com/MycroftAI/mimic3-voices/blob/master/LICENSE),
blob `2d58298e6eda10e7204abb52722efbc840db2390`). The two new synthetic clips are supplied under those same
terms, with this attribution; [LICENSE-voice.txt](LICENSE-voice.txt) contains the full terms. Their only processing
is the leading silence and WAV encoding described above. This fixture licence does not relicense the application
code. sherpa-onnx's Apache-2.0 and its phonemiser notices remain in the repository's existing packaging notices;
no model weights or new production dependency are distributed here.
